title: xiom test
concept: `xiom test` discovers and runs all test functions in a project
why: Manual verification doesn't scale. `xiom test` automates correctness checking: compile all tests, run them, and report failures. A single command gives you confidence that your code works. It's the foundation of continuous integration — if tests pass, the build is good.
theory: `xiom test` scans the project for functions marked with `@test` attribute or inside `test` modules. It compiles a test binary (separate from the main binary) that includes all test harnesses, runs each test in parallel (default: number of CPU cores), captures output, and reports a summary. Tests can be filtered with `xiom test <name_pattern>`. Test binaries link against the library target, so unit tests have access to private internals.
syntax_ref:
xiom test                    # run all tests
xiom test <filter>           # run matching tests
xiom test -- --nocapture     # show println output
xiom test -- --test-threads=1 # run sequentially
tips: Tests run in parallel by default — don't rely on execution order
common_mistakes: Writing tests that depend on shared mutable state (they run in parallel)
Forgetting the `@test` attribute so the function is never discovered
Using `assert` instead of `assert_eq` — `assert` requires a Bool expression
